target_audience.audience: Operations and transformation leaders at mid-market software companies

research_questions: What proof reduces perceived implementation risk?
What makes a workflow replacement feel relevant across teams?

evidence_sources.limits: Fictional, aggregate conformance evidence; not population prevalence.
Fictional, aggregate conformance evidence; not population prevalence.

findings.statement: Operations leaders seek an implementation mechanism and adoption proof before replacing core workflows.
findings.inference_boundary: Applies only to the bundled fictional buying context.
creative_implications: Show how the change works and what supports adoption.

findings.statement: Transformation leaders look for cross-team visibility and executive alignment without another disconnected layer.
findings.inference_boundary: Applies only to the bundled fictional buying context.
creative_implications: Connect the promise to shared visibility and coordinated action.

segment_hypotheses.name: Evidence-led operations leaders
segment_hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_ad_testing: They scrutinize implementation and adoption claims.

segment_hypotheses.name: Alignment-focused transformation leaders
segment_hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_ad_testing: They evaluate whether the promise connects teams and executive priorities.

privacy_confirmation.note: Only bundled fictional aggregate evidence is included.

approval.approval_note: Approved for the two-run synthetic conformance demonstration.
